answer: Social graph spectral analysis at the pearl layer: each agent's eigenvector centrality weights its vote, so buying identities adds little connectivity. The ridge of the second eigenvalue exposes clusters — fake accounts cluster tightly and inflate the Fiedler gap. Real trust flows like a vine through genuine edges, which sybils cannot cheaply fabricate. Attacker break-even: fabricating one credible trust edge costs roughly 50x a fresh identity, so a 100-node farm burns ~5,000 identity-equivalents before swaying one proposal — unprofitable versus honest yield.
